messages:
Sasha: Hey — noticed a ~12–15% tail latency regression on long contexts (2k-4k) after the FP8 rollout + new calib dataset. Using fp8-opt kernels on A100s. Anyone else seeing this?

Miguel: saw similar in nightly perf tests, but only when batch size > 4. Small batches look fine. Could be batching heuristics or KV cache churn.

perf-bot: nightly-profiling /models/llama-xx-large fp8-opt
cpu: 12% user, 5% sys
gpu kernel time breakdown:
 - attention_fp8_kernel: 62ms
 - kv_store: 14ms
 - batch_coalesce: 25ms
Tail99: 310ms -> 358ms (+15%)
(Attached flamegraph link: https://perf/redwood/1819456789)

Ana: two quick hypotheses:
1) FP8 kernels increase per-layer kernel launches -> worse scheduling for large batch+long seq
2) calibration dataset has long-tail prompts (few outliers) that push quant ranges and cause extra dequant ops
We should isolate by running same model with INT8 profile + same DS.

Tyler: also check KV cache hit density — with per-tensor quantization, small head differences cause key mismatches because we quantize/round differently across microbatches. Might force re-quant per step. I can run a trace to confirm.

Rachel: about calibration data — our current set includes 10k samples, scraped from web dialogs. A handful of outliers have huge token values (code dumps). I argue we should do trimmed calibration: drop top/bottom 1% per-channel. Per-channel calibration tends to be more robust for attention matrices.

Jin: per-channel vs per-tensor tradeoff:
- per-channel: better numeric for conv/linear but bigger metadata and slower memcpy patterns
- per-tensor: faster path, but more sensitive to outliers
Maybe use per-channel for QKV and per-tensor elsewhere. We need an automated rule in the optimizer.

Sasha: proposal: run ablation 3 runs:
A) FP8 kernels + current calib (10k full)
B) FP8 + trimmed calib (drop top/bottom 1%)
C) FP8 + per-channel for QKV only
Measure tail P95/P99 and batch coalesce time. Can someone own?

Miguel: I'll run A/B on the nightly rig. Starting now. cc @eng-runtime

Ana: I'll produce trimmed calibration script. Quick snippet:

I'll push to feature/calib-trim.

Tyler: i'll instrument kv hit rates + quant-requant counters in runtime. If we see extra re-quant ops that's the smoking gun.

perf-bot: scheduled jobs queued: nightly-ablate-181945 A/B/C. ETA ~2h.

Rachel: quick note — also watch quality delta (perplexity + a small eval set). Trimming can change dynamic range and hurt low-prob tokens.

Jin: agree, add small eval prompt set for QA and math prompts. We'll log logits differences.

Sasha: cool. Let's reconvene in ~3h in #eng-ml with results. Thanks :thumbsup:
